blocks.name: Travel Card
blocks.description: A two-stage travel booking card that morphs from a full-bleed poster into a detail view with price, tags, and an Add to Cart action.

variations.name: default
variations.description: The image, background color, CTA button, and a badge icon all animate between a cover-photo stage and a detail stage with price and tags, connected by an icon that flies along a curved path between the two.

props.name: imageUrl
props.description: Cover photo URL rendered in both stages. Defaults to the built-in Deep Blue Nights photo.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Alt text for the cover photo.

props.name: title
props.description: Destination/product title shown in the detail stage header.

props.name: description
props.description: Body copy shown below the title in the detail stage.

props.name: price
props.description: Price pill text, e.g. "$2,999".

props.name: availabilityText
props.description: Text in the top-right chip, e.g. "9 seats left".

props.name: tagText
props.description: Label on the icon pill next to the price, e.g. "Perfect for summer".

props.name: tagIcon
props.description: HugeIcons icon rendered inside the tag pill. Defaults to Sun01Icon.

props.name: exploreLabel
props.description: CTA label shown in the collapsed stage. Defaults to "Explore".

props.name: addToCartLabel
props.description: CTA label shown in the expanded stage. Defaults to "Add to Cart".

props.name: onAddToCart
props.description: Called when the CTA is clicked while the card is expanded (the Add to Cart action).

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the root wrapper.

variations.previewHint: Click Explore to expand the card, click Add to Cart to collapse it back
features: Image, card background, and CTA button all morph size/position/color together on a single click, driven by one shared stage state
A single icon travels along an SVG offset-path between the button and the detail chip so the two stages read as one continuous object, not a swap
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — all springs and the flight-path animation collapse to instant transitions

blocks.name: Theme Button
blocks.description: A pill button that morphs into a picker menu on click using a shared layoutId. Click the font name to choose a typeface or the color swatch to choose a theme. Fully configurable: pass your own themes/fonts (list or function), control the selection, and react to picks via onThemeChange/onFontChange. The shell springs open with an Apple-style expand/collapse, content cross-fades with a blur, and the whole surface is theme-token aware for light and dark.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Collapsed status pill morphs into an expanded font or theme list via a shared layoutId spring, with a blur cross-fade on the inner content. Themes/fonts, selection, and change callbacks are all props. Includes an inlined iOS pulse spinner so the block ships self-contained.

props.name: themes
props.description: Theme options as a list or a function returning one. Each: { id, label, dots: string[] }. Falls back to the built-in set.

props.name: fonts
props.description: Font options as a list or a function returning one. Each: { id, label, stack }. Falls back to the built-in set.

props.name: defaultThemeId
props.description: Uncontrolled initial theme selection, by id.

props.name: defaultFontId
props.description: Uncontrolled initial font selection, by id.

props.name: themeId
props.description: Controlled theme selection, by id. When set, the theme dimension is controlled.

props.name: fontId
props.description: Controlled font selection, by id. When set, the font dimension is controlled.

props.name: onThemeChange
props.description: Fires with the full option after a theme is picked — do whatever you want with it.

props.name: onFontChange
props.description: Fires with the full option after a font is picked.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when the menu opens ('font' | 'theme') or closes (null).

props.name: processLabel
props.description: Label shown next to the spinner segment.

props.name: showProcess
props.description: Show the spinner + label segment.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the pill shell.

variations.previewHint: Click the font name or the color swatch — the sample text below reacts to your pick
features: Morphs between collapsed pill and expanded menu via a shared layoutId — Motion interpolates size, position, and border-radius in one spring
Runs an asymmetric Apple-style spring: expand at 0.4s with slight bounce, collapse ~30% faster with none
Cross-fades inner content with a blur; exit runs ~25% faster than enter so old content clears before the morph lands
Implements the full APG menu pattern: role="menu" with menuitemradio options, roving tabindex, and focus returned to the opening trigger
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — the morph spring, cross-fade, and spinner all collapse to instant

blocks.name: Teletype Clock
blocks.description: A classic split-flap airport-board clock. Each digit lives on a dark card split by a center seam — when the time changes, the top flap falls with gravity, reveals the next digit, and the bottom flap lands with a mechanical bounce.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Four HH:MM digit cards. On change, the old digit's top half hinges down on the center seam (ease-in free fall), then the new digit's bottom half swings into place with an overshoot-and-settle bounce. Shading overlays darken the falling flap and light up the landing one for a 3D feel.

props.name: demo
props.description: Advance the clock by one minute on an interval so flips happen constantly (for showcases)

props.name: demoIntervalMs
props.description: Milliseconds between flips in demo mode

props.name: hour12
props.description: Use 12-hour format instead of 24-hour

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes for the outer wrapper

variations.previewHint: Digits flip every few seconds in demo mode
features: Two-phase flip: rotateX 0 → -90° fall with ease-in-cubic gravity, then 90 → 0° landing with overshoot bounce
Only transform and opacity are animated — flaps run on the compositor with backface-visibility hidden
Digit halves are full-height numerals clipped by overflow-hidden windows, so the seam cuts each digit cleanly
Lighting overlays: the falling flap darkens as it turns away, the landing flap brightens as it catches light
prefers-reduced-motion: digits swap instantly via useReducedMotion — no flap animation
Mounts at 00:00 and flips to the real time, doubling as an entrance animation with no hydration mismatch

blocks.name: SubItem Navbar
blocks.description: A morphing pill navbar anchored at the bottom. Each tab expands into either a chip filter row or any custom ReactNode panel — pass a login form, a settings menu, or anything else.

variations.name: subitem-navbar
variations.description: Tabs expand a panel above the bar via a spring-driven height animation. Panels are either a chip filter list (subs) or any React node (panel). LoginPanel is a named export for use as a panel slot.

props.name: items
props.description: Array of nav items passed to the bar.

props.name: items[].label
props.description: Tab label shown below the icon.

props.name: items[].icon
props.description: HugeIcons icon component rendered in the tab button.

props.name: items[].subs
props.description: Chip filter list. Mutually exclusive with panel.

props.name: items[].subs[].label
props.description: Chip label text.

props.name: items[].subs[].icon
props.description: Chip icon.

props.name: items[].panel
props.description: Custom panel rendered when the tab is active. Mutually exclusive with subs. Pass <LoginPanel /> or any component.

variations.previewHint: Tap any tab to expand its panel — Work/About/Journal show chip filters, Login shows a form
features: Discriminated union props: each NavItem has either subs (chip list) or panel (any ReactNode)
LoginPanel is a named export with self-contained email/password/showPassword state
Blur overlay rendered inside the component — just place BottomNavbar inside a relative container
useMeasure drives submenu height so the pill expands to exactly fit any panel
prefers-reduced-motion: all spring and blur transitions collapse to instant

blocks.name: Steps Count Block
blocks.description: A month of daily step counts in a bottom sheet. Tap a bar and it becomes a vertical slider you drag to set the count, with the fill colour interpolated in OKLCH along a red → amber → green ramp and a dashed rule at the 10,000 goal. A calendar popover adds days, a month select moves the window, and the whole chart re-scales on a spring when a drag lands.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A vaul bottom sheet wrapping a step-count chart. Each bar is a Base UI vertical slider whose fill is coloured by interpolating in OKLCH rather than sRGB, so the amber-to-green midpoint stays chromatic instead of collapsing to olive. The chart freezes its own scale for the duration of a drag so the bar tracks the finger exactly, then springs to the new ceiling on release. Days are added from a weekday-aligned calendar popover and removed from the header; the month select walks back twelve months. Every measurement is derived — the well's radius from the bars, the bar gap from how many days are on record, the sheet's radius from the card's.

props.name: children
props.description: Rendered as the trigger via `Drawer.Trigger asChild`. Omit it and drive the drawer with `open` / `onOpenChange` instead.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. When set, the drawer stops tracking its own — pair with onOpenChange.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires whenever the sheet opens or closes, including on a drag-dismiss from the handle and on Escape.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the card through cn, so its width, radius and padding can be overridden at the call site. The card defaults to `w-[420px] max-w-full`.

props.name: title
props.description: The sheet's accessible name. Visually hidden — the card's own header already says it on screen.

props.name: description
props.default: "A month of daily step counts. Tap a bar to select it, then drag to change the count."
props.description: The sheet's accessible description, announced on open. Visually hidden.

props.name: container
props.description: Portal target, defaulting to document.body. Pass an element and the sheet is portalled into it *and* switched from `fixed` to `absolute`, so it fills that element instead of the viewport — both halves are required, since a `fixed` child of a container is still laid out against the viewport. The container needs `position: relative` and `overflow: hidden`.

props.name: modal
props.description: `false` drops the scroll lock and the focus trap. Worth turning off when the sheet is demoed inside a page rather than owning the screen.

variations.previewHint: Tap the Steps button on the phone screen — the sheet rises inside the frame. Tap a bar to select it and drag its cap up and down to watch the fill travel the ramp; tap outside the sheet or drag the handle down to close.
features: `handleOnly` on the drawer is load-bearing rather than stylistic: vaul dismisses on a downward drag anywhere in its content, and the selected bar *is* a vertical drag target — without it, pulling a bar down to lower a count closes the sheet instead, and the one gesture the block exists for is the one gesture it cannot receive

The ramp is interpolated in OKLCH, not sRGB — a per-channel sRGB lerp between amber and green drives through the middle of the gamut where chroma collapses, and the midpoint came out #AA9D5F, a dull olive at *lower* chroma than either endpoint; in OKLCH the same midpoint is a chartreuse at 0.150, which is what actually sits between the two
Hue mixing takes the shortest way round the wheel, so 350° to 10° is 20° rather than 340°

The lit top of each bar's gradient is +0.09 lightness in OKLCH with chroma eased back, not a lerp toward white — mixing with white in sRGB desaturates and cools at once, which turned the terracotta end dusty pink
The scale freezes for the duration of a drag and springs to its new ceiling on release, so the bar under the finger tracks it exactly instead of rescaling out from under it

That release transition is gated on a 350ms `rescaling` window rather than left open on the element, because Base UI sizes the indicator from `max` — a blanket transition would also catch value changes and make every arrow-key press lag 350ms behind the keyboard

`bounce: 0` on every bar spring, in both the column's scaleY and the resting bar's height: an underdamped spring overshoots the value, and a bar that springs past its own height is drawing a step count nobody walked
The press state squeezes a bar narrower, never shorter — width carries no meaning on this chart, so it is the one axis free to move

Every radius is derived rather than picked: the bars set `--sc-r-bar`, the well clears them by `PLOT.inset`, and the sheet's top corners are the card's radius plus the gap between them, so changing one number moves the whole chain
Bar gap is a pure function of how many days are on record — six entries breathe at 10px, a fully logged month packs to 2px — and bar *width* is never set at all, since the columns are `flex-1`
One dashed rule, at the goal. There were four evenly spaced at quarters of a moving ceiling, so they marked nothing; meanwhile the card was colouring every bar against a threshold it never drew

One popover for the whole chart, re-anchored to whichever bar is selected, rather than 31 popovers that are all closed — and the resolved anchor element is held in state, because Base UI resolves `anchor` once on open and an inline getter would go stale the moment the selection moved

The bar ref's cleanup checks element identity, because a column swapping between resting bar and slider mounts the incoming ref before running the outgoing one's cleanup — an unguarded cleanup clears the fresh element
The add-day calendar is weekday-aligned with leading pad cells, so the 14th sits in its real column instead of wherever arithmetic put it

Every colour is a namespaced `--sc-*` custom property consumed from Tailwind arbitrary values, so the palette has one definition and the markup stays classes rather than a `style` prop on every second element; the namespace is what keeps it from writing to a host app's `--ink` or `--hover`

MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" covers the Motion half and `motion-reduce:transition-none` covers the CSS half — including the inline rescale transition, which is guarded in its ternary because only an `!important` class could outrank an inline style

Closes on an outside press or a drag on the handle, and the sheet's gutter is one number on all four sides so the radius chain actually holds — the sheet's corner is the card's corner plus that gap. The handle is centred *inside* the top gutter rather than stacked above the card, because in flow it added its own height and margin to the top padding and made the one edge nobody had measured the one that looked deliberate

Every portalled root republishes the `--sc-*` palette, without exception — custom properties inherit down the DOM and a portal leaves the card's subtree entirely, so a class like `bg-[var(--sc-ink)] text-white` inside one fails to a transparent box with white text rather than to a visible fallback

Overrides vaul's 500ms open/close down to 260ms in and 200ms out, keeping vaul's own `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` — the steep iOS-sheet start is what lets the duration come down that far without the motion reading as a cut, and the asymmetry is there because a sheet on its way out has already been dismissed

Every override out-specifies the vaul rule it replaces by one attribute rather than relying on stylesheet order, since vaul injects its CSS at module load; the stylesheet is hoisted and de-duplicated by React on `href`, so two mounted sheets yield one <style>

Reduced motion swaps the sheet's `animation-name` to a fade rather than disabling it — gentler, not zero. `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` covers Motion only, and vaul's open/close is CSS keyframes that ran a full-height slide regardless

blocks.name: Question Builder Modal
blocks.description: A two-level modal: a grid of eight question types drills into a per-type settings form, and the panel springs to the height of whatever screen is showing. The corner element morphs from a rounded badge into a back button through a shared layoutId rather than crossfading, so the chrome reads as one object changing role.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A two-level modal built on shadcn's Dialog inspired by Luma modal transition.

props.name: children
props.description: Rendered as the trigger via DialogTrigger asChild. Omit it and drive the modal with `open` / `onOpenChange` instead.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. When set, the modal stops tracking its own state — pair with onOpenChange.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires whenever the modal opens or closes, including on submit and on Escape.

props.name: onAddQuestion
props.description: Fires on submit with { type, question, required, settings }. `settings` is per-type — e.g. { length } for text, { allowMultiple, options } for options, { contentType, showBeforeAccept, collectSignature } for terms.

props.name: title
props.description: Picker headline, the step screens' centered title, and the dialog's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.default: "Ask guests custom questions when they register."
props.description: Sub-headline under the picker title, and the dialog's accessible description.

props.name: types
props.description: Replaces or reorders the type grid. Each: { id, label, description, icon, defaultQuestion }. `id` must stay within QuestionTypeId, since it selects which form the step screen renders.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the dialog panel through cn, so panel width, radius and padding can be overridden at the call site.

variations.previewHint: Open it, pick a type, then use the corner button to go back — watch the panel height and the corner badge morph together
features: Two screens in one panel: an eight-tile type grid drills into that type's settings form, with direction derived from depth so back and forward are never confused — one `navigate` call writes both the view and the direction, which is what makes them impossible to desync

The panel animates to the measured height of whatever screen is showing, measured on an element *inside* the animated one so the reading is always the natural height and never chases its own animation

The base `zoom-in-95` entrance is overridden to `zoom-in-100` at the call site, because a bounding-rect measurement is transform-aware — under the stock zoom the first height reading lands mid-animation at 95% and sticks

The corner badge and the back button are a single element sharing a layoutId, so the box, its corner radius and its size morph as one object; the radius is set in `style` rather than a class, since a CSS-set radius is invisible to Motion's layout projection and gets stretched with the box
The glyph inside carries its own `layout` prop, which counter-scales it so it stays optically correct while the box around it is mid-morph
Header title and body screens share one variant set and one duration, so the two titles travel with identical physics rather than being tuned twice

Every shadcn primitive is used exactly as installed — Dialog, Button, Input, Textarea, Label, Switch — and restyled only through className at the call site, so `npx shadcn add` never has to overwrite a base component and later shadcn updates do not conflict

The ghost close button explicitly clears this style's gradient background-image and shadow with arbitrary properties, because those sit in different tailwind-merge groups to the flat token background and would otherwise render on top of each other

Every colour is a namespaced --qd-* token defined as `var(--theme-token, literal)`, so the modal inherits a host app's palette where one exists and still renders standalone where none does — and it never writes to the consumer's base tokens
Light and dark ship different shadow and raised-surface values rather than one black-alpha shadow that vanishes against a dark panel
Focus rings run on --ring rather than a 15%-alpha foreground, which falls under the 3:1 contrast minimum for non-text UI and reads as decoration instead of focus
The picker's corner badge is `disabled` rather than aria-hidden — a hidden-but-focusable control is an accessibility failure, and on the picker the element genuinely has no action
MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" wraps the whole surface, so every transform animation collapses for anyone who asked for less motion

blocks.name: Profile Card
blocks.description: An avatar that morphs into a full profile card using shared layout animation. Click the avatar to expand; click anywhere to dismiss.

variations.name: navbar
variations.description: Small avatar in a phone frame expands via layoutId into a floating profile card with staggered menu groups.

props.name: name
props.description: Display name shown in the expanded card header.

props.name: email
props.description: Email shown below the name in the expanded card header.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Avatar slot rendered both collapsed (36px) and expanded (42px). Defaults to DefaultAvatar. Pass an , next/image, or any node.

props.name: menuItems
props.description: Flat list of menu rows. Defaults to the built-in Profile/Community/Subscription/Settings/Help/Sign out set.

props.name: menuItems[].label
props.description: Row label text.

props.name: menuItems[].icon
props.description: HugeIcons icon component rendered in the row.

props.name: menuItems[].badge
props.description: Trailing slot — pass a count pill, a PRO badge, or any node.

props.name: menuItems[].active
props.description: Highlights the row background.

props.name: menuItems[].onClick
props.description: Click handler for the row.

props.name: menuItems[].dividerAfter
props.description: Renders a full-width divider below this row — used to group rows without needing a nested array.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the root wrapper.

variations.previewHint: Tap the avatar in the top-right to expand the profile card
features: Two shared layout transitions run in parallel on one duration spring (duration 0.5, bounce 0.25): layoutId "profile-card" projects the box from 40px to 310px while layoutId "profile-avatar" carries the avatar as its own child, so the avatar interpolates 36px to 42px as a circle instead of stretching with the widening container — one continuous morph, no clone or swap

Header text and menu rows live in a fade wrapper decoupled from the morph: opacity and a blur(4px) to blur(0px) filter animate on an ease-out tween delayed 0.18s, so content resolves into a card that has already settled rather than smearing during the layout projection

A menuReady gate holds the rows pointer-events-none for 400ms (the fade's 0.18s delay plus 0.2s duration) after open, so a fast press or the opening click's mouse-up can't activate a row while it is still invisible

splitIntoSegments derives dividers from a flat menuItems array: a per-row dividerAfter flag starts a new group, keeping badge, active-row highlight, and onClick as composable per-item slots without a nested array shape

Dismiss is an AnimatePresence overlay pinned absolute inset-0 to the component's own box (fades 0.15s) with the collapsed trigger switched to pointerEvents none while open; rows give a whileTap scale-0.98 press and focus as native motion.buttons, though the menu ships pointer-first with no role="menu" contract or prefers-reduced-motion fallback yet

blocks.name: Product Card

variations.name: default
variations.description: Three photos morph from an overlapping stacked deck into an evenly spaced fan, while the CTA morphs from a small gallery icon into a full-width action button and the price/description/tags fade in.

props.name: images
props.description: The three photo URLs rendered in the stacked deck and fan layouts.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Base alt text for each photo; suffixed with its position (e.g. "Product photo 1").

props.name: title
props.description: Product/listing title shown in the expanded stage.

props.name: description
props.description: Body copy shown below the title in the expanded stage.

props.name: price
props.description: Price pill text, e.g. "$189/night".

props.name: tags
props.description: Pill labels rendered below the description in the expanded stage.

props.name: viewLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the CTA while collapsed (icon-only button).

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: CTA label shown in the expanded stage. Defaults to "Book Now".

props.name: viewIcon
props.description: HugeIcons icon rendered in the collapsed, icon-only CTA. Defaults to GridViewIcon.

props.name: actionIcon
props.description: HugeIcons icon rendered next to the CTA label in the expanded stage. Defaults to ShoppingBag01Icon.

props.name: onAction

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the root wrapper.

variations.previewHint: Click the gallery icon to expand the card, click Book Now to collapse it back
features: Three photos animate independently between a stacked deck and an evenly spaced fan on a single click
CTA morphs between an icon-only button and a full-width labeled button, driven by the same stage state as the photos
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — all springs and detail transitions collapse to instant transitions

blocks.name: Pixel Dissolve Card
blocks.description: An editorial card whose cover photo dissolves into a grid of pixels to reveal the next slide, with the heading fading up beneath it.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Clicking the card swaps the image underneath instantly, then dissolves the outgoing photo away as a size × size grid of tiles. Each tile is a background-position slice of the same image, and tiles are assigned to random groups so they vanish in scattered clusters instead of sweeping row by row.

props.name: slides
props.description: Ordered list of slides cycled through on click. Defaults to three built-in editorial slides.

props.name: slides[].image
props.description: Cover photo URL for the slide.

props.name: slides[].imageAlt
props.description: Alt text for the cover photo. Defaults to an empty string (decorative).

props.name: slides[].heading
props.description: Headline shown in the card body under the photo.

props.name: size
props.description: Grid resolution of the dissolve — renders size × size tiles.

props.name: revealStep
props.description: Seconds between each tile group vanishing. Total dissolve length is roughly size × revealStep.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the card root.

variations.previewHint: Click the card to advance — the current photo dissolves pixel by pixel into the next one
features: The incoming image is rendered underneath from the first frame, so the dissolve reveals the next slide rather than a blank gap
Every tile is the same image positioned by background-position on a size×size background — one network request, no canvas, no image slicing
Cells are bucketed into `size` random groups of `size` cells each, and the groups are given randomized delays, so tiles disappear in scattered clusters instead of a predictable sweep
Tiles are overscaled by 1.02 to hide the hairline seams that subpixel grid rounding otherwise leaves between them
Clicks are ignored while a dissolve is in flight, and the cleanup timeout is cleared on unmount
Rendered as a real <button> with an aria-label, and the tile grid is aria-hidden so screen readers only ever see the current slide

The heading crossfades rather than swapping: the old copy lifts and fades out over 180ms while the new one reveals word by word from behind a clipping mask, 20ms apart via motion/react variants, so the text resolves alongside the image
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — the dissolve is skipped entirely and the slide swaps instantly

blocks.name: Onboarding Form
blocks.description: Multi-step onboarding form with a vertical ticker step indicator on the left and an animated question panel on the right, covering five field types: radio, dropdown, multi-select, short text and long text.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Multi-step onboarding form with a vertical ticker step indicator on the left and an animated question panel on the right, covering five field types: radio, dropdown, multi-select, short text and long text.

props.name: steps
props.description: Array of { label, question, type?, options?, placeholder?, optional? } objects defining each step. type is one of "radio" | "select" | "multi" | "text" | "textarea" and defaults to "radio"; options is required for radio, select and multi; optional lets the user skip the step and shows a Skip button

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Callback fired when the user submits the final step, receives Record<number, string | string[]> keyed by step index — "multi" steps answer with string[], every other type with string

variations.previewHint: Answer each step — radio, dropdown, multi-select, then text — and click the arrow to advance
features: Five field types in one form — radio, dropdown, multi-select, short text and long text — each chosen by the shape of its question, so swapping them into your own steps is a data change
Vertical ticker syncs with the active step, and completed steps compress and tick off so the remaining path visibly shortens
Progress bar across the card gives progress one owner, with a real progressbar role for assistive tech
Question panel slides in/out with direction-aware animation (forward vs back)
Steps can be marked optional — a Skip button appears and validation is bypassed
Every field takes its accessible name from the visible question heading — no placeholder is ever the label
Next stays enabled: submitting without an answer surfaces a type-specific error, with icon and colour, and moves focus to the field
Long-text steps submit with ⌘/Ctrl + Enter, since Enter inserts a newline
Completion screen reflects every answer back, and takes focus so the result is announced
Light and dark themes via --onb-* tokens, every foreground/background pair measured with APCA
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — all transitions collapse to duration 0

blocks.name: Morphing Image Effect
blocks.description: A click-driven 3-stage animation where a typographic split ('P' | image | 'ST') morphs between states — the image pill reshapes and the text scales on each click.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Three-stage morph: thumbnail pill → landscape card → portrait card. Text scales inversely as the image grows.
variations.previewHint: Click anywhere to advance through the 3 stages
features: CSS t-resize class owns width/height transitions so layout reflow stays on the compositor thread
Framer Motion animate handles borderRadius and rotate — no layout thrashing
Stage label uses AnimatePresence mode='wait' with blur cross-fade
prefers-reduced-motion: t-resize transition is disabled via media query
Single Image element reused across all stages — no clone, no re-mount

blocks.name: Frosted Navbar
blocks.description: A sticky, glass-like navbar with a uniform backdrop blur clipped cleanly to its own bounds, plus an optional lit edge-highlight rim along the bottom.

variations.name: frosted-navbar
variations.description: No hardcoded height or width: the bar sizes to its content and its parent's width, so it drops into any layout as a <nav> or <header>. The blur layer extends past the nav's own edge for clean filter sampling, then gets clipped by overflow-hidden so it never bleeds into content below.

props.name: as
props.description: Element/tag to render as. Defaults to "nav"; use "header" for page chrome.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the bar: nav links, icons, a search input, a card title, etc.

props.name: blur
props.description: Blur strength in px for the main backdrop region. Defaults to 12.

props.name: brightness
props.description: Brightness percentage applied to the main backdrop filter. Defaults to 110.

props.name: saturate
props.description: Saturation percentage applied to the main backdrop filter. Defaults to 110.

variations.previewHint: The cluster enters outward from the mark — hover any avatar to lift it and turn it to colour
features: Ships its own namespaced colour tokens, each defined as the theme token with a literal fallback — the cluster inherits a host theme where one exists and still renders correctly in a project with no token layer, without ever overwriting the consumer's own `--background` or `--foreground`

Colour comes from the theme's semantic tokens (background, foreground, muted, border, ring) rather than hardcoded neutrals, so the cluster themes with whatever app installs it instead of imposing its own greys

Once a member is active the rest of the faces step back to 50% opacity, so the selected person reads across the whole layout rather than only inside the grid; at rest nothing is dimmed, which keeps the cluster a group portrait instead of a permanently deselected list
Every literal ink — hatch, shadows, conic edge, radial mask — is written in OKLCH, matching the project's token layer

Opt-in role badges sit outside the hover layer, so the pill never inherits the tile's 1.08 lift and scale its text; they are also pointer-events-none, since a badge that intercepts the hover that summoned it flickers forever
Badge side is derived from the tile's column relative to the centre, so a badge on a left-hand tile points inward rather than off the edge of the grid

Badge side points inward on the outermost columns and away from the centre elsewhere, so a badge never leaves the grid — which is what a compact 3-wide layout, where every tile is an edge tile, would otherwise do

The caller's `renderBadge` is invoked inside the badge component, not in the grid: calling opaque code with a member in the grid's scope makes the React Compiler treat `members` as possibly mutated and drop every memo derived from it

Selection is controllable: pass `selectedId` and `onSelect` and the grid stops holding its own copy, so a role list rendered beside it and the grid itself write to one piece of state instead of two that drift

Hover previews and click commits, split the way contact-reveal-card does it, so a touch user can select a member at all; `onActiveChange` reports the result outward and lets a section render the details without the grid knowing how they are laid out

The cluster enters as a wave outward from the brand mark — tiles are grouped into rings by their distance from the centre so equidistant members arrive together, which reads as one expanding gesture rather than six unrelated fades
Entrance and interaction live on two nested layers: the outer owns a delayed tween, the inner owns an interruptible spring, so the entrance delay never leaks into a hover
Colour and lift share timing — the grayscale transition was retuned from Tailwind's default 300ms curve to 200ms ease-out-quad so the two halves of one hover land together
Reduced motion keeps the fade and the colour change but drops every scale: the entrance still explains the layout, it just stops moving to say so
Hover is gated on a real pointer in both CSS and JS — touch fires hover on tap with nothing to un-fire it, which would strand a tapped tile lifted and in colour
Empty tiles are derived from rows × columns minus the occupied cells, so the placeholder backdrop refills itself when the grid or the member list changes
The placeholder shells sit on their own masked layer that mirrors the parent's tracks and gap, so the circular fade can dissolve the outer hatching without dimming the avatars stacked above it
Placeholder tiles carry their own grid placement rather than sitting in a wrapper — a wrapper stretches to the track while the tile inside keeps auto height and collapses to a single dashed line

Tile depth is a three-layer transparent box-shadow rather than a border — a 1px ring layer plus two soft lift layers — so the tiles hold up over any background the block is dropped onto; dark mode collapses to a single white ring since soft black depth is invisible there

Photo edges use an inset `outline` rather than a border or ring: it follows the border-radius, adds nothing to layout, and is pure black/white at 10% — a tinted neutral would pick up the surface underneath and read as dirt on the edge

The brand tile — the only one with no photo to define its own edge — gets a conic gradient masked down to a 1px band instead, two masks (border box and content box) composited with `exclude` erasing the middle

That conic starts at 45deg so its stops land exactly on the four corners, alternating light and dark; the inks are theme variables, and in dark mode both go white so the alternation comes from alpha rather than hue, since a black ink is invisible on the dark tile
The brand mark's optical centring is corrected in the SVG path itself, not with a nudge in the component, so the icon stays centred wherever it is reused
The hovered tile raises its z-index for the whole spring, so the lifted avatar never slides under a neighbouring tile mid-animation
Grayscale-to-colour runs as a CSS filter transition while the lift runs on a spring, so the two read as one gesture without animating a filter on the main thread every frame

blocks.name: AI Chat
blocks.description: An AI prompt composer built around a light input card floating over an inverse-shell control row. The mode and model pickers morph from pill to panel via shared layoutId springs, the plus button fans a radial attachment menu, the tool chips stagger in with a cross-blur, and the mic swaps to a live waveform while a typewriter transcript slides in above. Every list — attachments, tools, modes, models, transcript phrases — is a prop, selection is controlled or uncontrolled per dimension, and the whole surface is driven by globals.css theme tokens so it flips cleanly between light and dark.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A theme-token-driven AI prompt composer. Mode and model pickers morph between a collapsed pill and an expanded panel through a shared layoutId spring with a blur cross-fade; the plus button fans out a radial attachment menu; tool chips reveal with a staggered cross-blur; the mic cross-fades to an animated waveform while a typewriter transcript slides in. Attachments, tools, modes, models, and transcript phrases are all props, with controlled/uncontrolled selection per dimension. The pickers ship as full APG menus (roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, focus restore), every control carries an accessible name, closed reveals are inert, the transcript announces through an aria-live region, and all motion honors prefers-reduced-motion.

variations.previewHint: Open the plus (radial attachments), the sparkle (tool chips), and the mode/model pills (morphing panels), then tap the mic to watch it swap to a waveform with a typewriter transcript
features: Morphs the mode and model pickers between a collapsed pill and an expanded panel via a shared layoutId, springing size, position, and border-radius in one motion while the inner content cross-fades through a blur
Fans the plus button's attachment items out along an arc from per-item sin/cos offsets, rotating the trigger 45° and staggering each item on a stiffness/damping spring

Reveals tool chips with a reverse-stagger panel drop — y-translate plus a 2px cross-blur on the transitions-dev ease — and swaps the sparkle glyph for the selected tool's icon through an AnimatePresence popLayout cross-fade
Cross-fades the mic into a height-keyframe waveform and slides a typewriter transcript panel in above the input, dimming the heading, input, and controls to 0.35 while recording

Implements the mode and model dropdowns as full APG menus — role="menu" with menuitemradio options, aria-checked selection, roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End navigation, Escape, and focus moved into the panel on open then returned to the trigger on close

Ships the accessibility contract with the block: accessible names on every icon-only control, a visually hidden label for the prompt, aria-expanded disclosures whose closed reveals are inert, an aria-live transcript region, and a prefers-reduced-motion fallback across the morph, waveform, caret, and typewriter
